## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** in automatic-location mode, the panel label now comes from the same `format=j1` report as the conditions, unit choice and Open-Meteo forecast coordinates, which resolves the mismatch described in #12904. No correctness issue was found in the changed code. Configured locations still take precedence, and no remaining code references `wttrLocation` or `locationProc`.

Label source for the #12904 data (no `weather.json`):

| | Label | Conditions |
|---|---|---|
| Base | `%l` request: Tel Aviv | j1 `nearest_area`: Orient, Illinois |
| Head | j1 `nearest_area`: Orient | j1 `nearest_area`: Orient, Illinois |

Each automatic refresh also makes one fewer wttr.in request. The added `weather-test.sh` assertions pass on the head and the new test fails on the base code at its first new assertion.

**Label change for auto-detect users:** the `%l` label was introduced in commit `048a7302` ("Use the more accurate location and tweak the look"); before it, the panel showed `areaInfo.areaName[0].value`, which is what this PR restores. Auto-detect users whose provider `nearest_area` differs from their IP-lookup city will now see that nearby area name instead of their city. That is the behavior #12904 asks for; how often the two differ was not established.

### CLI and right-click status still name the `%l` location

After this change, other surfaces still derive the automatic place from `https://wttr.in/?format=%l`:

```text
Surface (no weather.json)        Place source                              #12904 responses
Panel                            j1 nearest_area                           Orient
omarchy weather location         %l  (bin/omarchy-weather-location:22-25)  Tel Aviv
Right-click notification         omarchy-weather-status: %l name, then     Tel Aviv
  (BarWidget.qml:78)             a separate wttr.in/<name>?format=%t|%w
                                 query for that name
```

`manual/10-notices.md:17` also tells users to run `omarchy weather location` "to see where it thinks you are".

**Impact:** in the #12904 scenario, the panel and the CLI/right-click notification would name different places. Each surface pairs its own name with weather queried for that name, so this is not a correctness regression in the panel. The place printed by `omarchy weather location` no longer describes the panel's weather, which can confuse a user checking the manual's advice.

**Suggested change:** decide which place source the automatic surfaces should share. For example, derive the no-argument `omarchy weather location` output from the j1 `nearest_area` as well, or state in the manual that the command reports the IP-detected place. This can be done here or as a follow-up. Replacing only the notification label while keeping its separate query would reintroduce a name/weather mismatch there.

**Optional test improvement:** the new assertion `/reportLocation.*areaInfo.*areaName/` also passes on the unfixed base, because the old binding contained the same identifiers in a different order. The other two assertions match identifier names, so a renamed separate `%l` lookup would still pass all three. Moving the label selection into a small `Model.js` function and asserting it against a j1 fixture shaped like #12904 (no configured name, `nearest_area` "Orient", expect "Orient"; with a configured name, expect that name) would test the behavior rather than the spelling.

**Test scope:** Source review of the head and base panel, CLI weather scripts, bar widget, manual and tests, plus wttr.in public source. `test/shell.d/weather-test.sh` was run in an isolated sandbox on head and base using a Deno-backed `node` shim, not Node itself. No Quickshell UI was run and wttr.in was not contacted, so rendered output and live provider responses were not observed.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
